note: اور is primarily the conjunction 'and' and also means more/other/another. Noun POS is misleading for the learner-facing entry.
ہیں is the plural/honorific present form of ہونا ('are'). Interjection POS is dictionary noise for this standard Urdu learner entry.

پر is the postposition on/at/upon and can also be a conjunction 'but/yet'; the same spelling also represents the noun feather/wing (پَر). Noun POS is currently unexplained and adjective POS is unnecessary.
proposed_english: on; at; upon; but/yet; feather/wing (پَر, context-dependent)

note: لئے is a form of لینا meaning taken, and it appears in the compound postposition کے لیے 'for'. Verb-only POS does not account for the learner gloss 'for'.
گیا is overwhelmingly the masculine singular perfect form of جانا ('went/gone/left') in ordinary Urdu. The proper noun Gaya should not lead the learner definition.
proposed_english: went; gone/left (masculine singular perfect of جانا); Gaya (proper noun, context-dependent)

note: جو is a relative pronoun meaning who/which/that, not a noun in this use.
و is the conjunction 'and' (Persian/Arabic-origin linker in Urdu). 'Character' is implementation metadata, not a learner POS.
گا is the masculine singular future marker/suffix, not merely an unspecified 'closed-class' item.
جب introduces or asks about time ('when') and functions as an adverbial/subordinating conjunction; adverb-only POS is incomplete.
اپنے is the masculine plural/oblique form of اپنا and functions as a reflexive possessive determiner/adjective. 'Closed-class' is too vague for learner grammar.
proposed_english: one's own; own (masculine plural/oblique form of اپنا)

note: جس is the oblique singular relative pronoun corresponding to جو. 'Closed-class' is too vague and hides its grammatical role.
دیا can be the noun lamp and, very commonly, the masculine singular perfect form of دینا ('gave/given'). Noun-only POS is incorrect.
proposed_english: gave; given (masculine singular form of دینا); lamp

note: تک is a postposition/particle meaning until, up to, or as far as. 'Closed-class' is not an adequate learner POS.
proposed_english: until; up to; as far as

note: گے is the masculine plural/honorific future marker. Noun POS is incorrect.
اپنی is the feminine form of اپنا and functions as a reflexive possessive determiner/adjective. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
proposed_english: one's own; own (feminine form of اپنا)

note: بہت centrally means very, much, many, or a lot. 'Enough/sufficient' is not an appropriate core gloss and the adjective-only POS misses its common adverb/quantifier use.
